summary: Weekly POC sync focussed on newly generated network heatmap, intermittent egress latency spikes during canary, kernel upgrade impact, and risk tradeoffs between hosted fallback and dedicated on-prem capacity. Team agreed to run a controlled rollback rehearsal and to capture traceroutes and firewall rules for deeper analysis.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-10
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sarah Liu (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Ethan Park (Solutions) — Lina Park (Aurelian PM), Tom Reynolds (Aurelian Infra), Jasper Cole (Aurelian CTO), Rita Menon (Aurelian Security), Mike O'Neill (Aurelian Dev)

Summary: quick walk through of network heatmap artifacts, three observed latency spikes on canary routes at 02:14/02:37/03:05 UTC, discussion about MTU and jumbo frames, suggestion of kernel-backed optimization rollback, and next steps to collect traceroutes and firewall/export logs.

[00:00] Sarah Liu: okay everyone, thanks for joining, we got a packed sync — Marco will run the heatmap and then we can triage the spikes, Lina you had flagged the first spike?
[00:12] Lina Park: yeah thanks Sarah, quick thing — we saw the first big tail at 02:14 during our load window, it looked like packet fragmentation maybe? but the team wasn't 100% sure.
[00:22] Marco Diaz: right, we generated the heatmap this morning, it overlays p50/p95/p99 latency per egress hop. i pulled the canary traces and there's a repeated 8-12ms bump before the transit gateway hop, which points to either MTU mismatch or microbursts on the firewall.
[00:40] Tom Reynolds: we did change the firewall ACLs last week, also bumped up anti-ddos signature scanning. that coincides with the timing. could be inspection pause.
[00:50] Jasper Cole: just to be clear, the infrastructure path is our VPC -> TGW -> partner transit -> redwood private peering. if any of those inspect packets with deep packet inspection there's CPU context switches, yeah it adds latency.
[01:05] Marco Diaz: one weird thing — the KV cache warmup on the Redwood side shows an extra 15–20ms on first token for some sessions, but subsequent tokens are fine. so initial handshake + egress queuing compound.
[01:24] Mike O'Neill: are we sure handshake is not TLS renegotiation? we saw a few TLS alerts in the logs but couldn't tie them.
[01:33] Rita Menon: security here — TLS renegotiation would be a red flag for us, but logs were inconclusive. we'll export the full TLS session logs after the call.
[01:45] Sarah Liu: good. Marco, on the kernel upgrade you rolled last week — did you observe any link flapping or offload changes?
[01:53] Marco Diaz: yes small change — we enabled GRO/LRO offload tweaks on a subset of nodes to reduce CPU per packet; in testing this reduced throughput CPU but it can interact badly with jumbo frames when MTU isn't matched. i suspect an offload mismatch.
[02:12] Tom Reynolds: we don't use jumbo frames broadly, only on some racks. maybe that mismatch is the root cause.
[02:21] Ethan Park: i worry more about the fallback routing — we saw a test where traffic shifted to the hosted fallback and p99 jumped by 60ms for a subset. we should quantify cost vs latency for keeping fallback turned on during spikes.
[02:33] Lina Park: cost is definitely a factor. our SRE lead wants predictable SLAs, they'd consider dedicated capacity if cost delta is manageable.
[02:42] Sarah Liu: noted. Marco — can you put together a small paper that shows expected token-cost delta for a dedicated fallback kept for 12 hours/day vs ad-hoc?
[02:50] Marco Diaz: yes, i'll include batching/kv cache effects and note quantization changes.
[02:58] [03:00] Speaker 6: (muffled) also want to call out BGP flap detected earlier — might be noise in traceroute
[03:08] Marco Diaz: good catch, that was a short BGP withdraw at 02:37, the heatmap shows a simultaneous spike — likely route churn. we need the partner transit logs to confirm.
[03:22] Jasper Cole: we're pushing for multi-path to avoid single transit dependency, but partner doesn't support ECMP reliably on that leg.
[03:31] Sarah Liu: okay action: Tom will collect partner contact and traceroutes for the 02:37 window.
[03:35] Tom Reynolds: yes i'll pull traceroutes and netflow and send by Friday.
[03:40] Lina Park: and we'll also share the updated firewall rule set, there are some lingering legacy NAT rules.
[03:45] Rita Menon: security will also export audit logs and the KMS rotation schedule. Jasper, remind — are we comfortable sharing KMS metadata with Redwood?
[03:54] Jasper Cole: we will share metadata and key IDs, not the raw keys. Redwood's KMS integration was in the docs, right Sarah?
[04:02] Sarah Liu: yes we support KMS/HSM integrations and we never ask for customer private keys. we'll accept wrapped keys and audit logs. we'll share the security package link after the call.
[04:12] Marco Diaz: back to perf — i propose a controlled kernel rollback on a canary pool during off-peak. revert the GRO/LRO tweaks and run the same synthetic test with jumbo frames disabled. that should prove/disprove the offload mismatch hypothesis.
[04:27] Tom Reynolds: fine, but we need a rehearsal runbook because our infra team got surprised last time and it caused a brief compaction event.
[04:36] Sarah Liu: yes we'll provide a rollback rehearsal plan. Ethan, can Redwood run the rehearsal and allow customer to shadow?
[04:42] Ethan Park: absolutely, we'll run in a mirrored canary and provide live logs and metrics.
[04:47] Marco Diaz: also i'll produce a heatmap delta comparing pre-upgrade, post-upgrade, and today so the team can visually inspect where latencies clustered.
[04:57] Lina Park: that visual diff would be super helpful. can you annotate which hops are owned by us vs partner vs redwood?
[05:05] Marco Diaz: yes i'll annotate ownership where we have it and mark unknowns.
[05:12] Mike O'Neill: one more dev note — we noticed a tokenization variance between quantized model and float model in internal evals, not related to routing but affects fallback quality. if traffic moves to a smaller quantized fallback, we need to track quality regressions.
[05:27] Sarah Liu: perfect segue — we'll add a small eval harness to capture model output diffs at canary sample rates. Priya will own that with your dev team.
[05:36] Priya Rao: noted, i'll share a template eval set by end of week so you can plug it in.
[05:42] Jasper Cole: regarding compliance, we need proof that audit logs will be retained in-country for certain datasets. Rita will coordinate specific datasets.
[05:51] Rita Menon: yes, i'll send an annotated list of regulated data categories; expect that Monday.
[05:58] Sarah Liu: walk-through of next steps: Marco to generate annotated heatmap and token-cost delta, Tom to provide traceroute/netflow and partner contact, Rita to share regulated dataset list and TLS logs, Redwood to share security docs and KMS integration guide, and schedule kernel rollback rehearsal week of Jan 24.
[06:18] Tom Reynolds: quick Q — what's the recommended default MTU from Redwood side for private peering?
[06:24] Marco Diaz: we recommend 1500 unless you're using jumbo end-to-end and have confirmed MTU on all transit hops; otherwise stick to 1500 to avoid fragmentation.
[06:31] (crosstalk)
[06:40] Sarah Liu: okay everyone, we'll capture these in the ticket and share artifacts. any blockers?
[06:45] Lina Park: non-blocker, timeline is fine as long as rehearsal is scheduled before Feb 1.
[06:50] Jasper Cole: same, if we can have rehearsal and postmortem within two weeks that's good.
[06:55] Sarah Liu: great thanks — we'll circle back in the next weekly unless anything urgent pops up.

End of transcript.

References and links mentioned:
- Heatmap export (will be uploaded to shared drive)
- Security package (Redwood KMS/HSM integration guide)
- Kernel rollback rehearsal plan (draft to be shared)
questions: Can Redwood keep fallback on with predictable cost impact?
What exact packet inspection rule caused the pause?
Will partner transit support ECMP for multi-path resiliency?
